utterances.text: When, at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina, a decision was made to establish a new Territorial Defence, and as far as I can remember, the media published this decision around the 8th or 9th of April, 1992. I can't be very precise about the date, but I remember this piece of information well that the existing Territorial Defence was being abolished and a new TO of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina established. It was this Crisis Staff which was established in Prud which initiated and held certain meetings in order to establish a new Territorial Defence staff and select a new leadership for the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just tell us whether the new leaders were selected? And we'll discuss it later.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, new leaders were elected, a new commander, a new chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was selected as the commander?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marko Bozanovic, who was a captain first class, I think, and the new chief of staff was Mr. Alija Fitozovic. The decision was made at a meeting of the joint Crisis Staff in the village of Grebnice, which is about five or six kilometres away from Samac, around the 12th or the 13th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zaric. We will now move on to a completely different topic. What do you know about the activities of the Serbian Democratic Party on the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac? In your intelligence work, what did you learn about the activities of the Serbian Democratic Party in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Democratic Party, on the area of Bosanski Samac municipality, and I would say further afield, followed part of the policy of its headquarters in Sarajevo. When I say this, I have to mention a fact which contributed to this polarisation, that is, that on the 14th of April [as interpreted], the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina held a session at which a decision was made, as far as I can recall, to the effect that Bosnia and Herzegovina should be declared an independent state and that it should not remain within Yugoslavia. This decision was supported by MPs from the HDZ and the SDA --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... I heard that Mr. Zaric was mentioning the 14th of October, not 14th of April, as it is here in the transcript on page 45, line 24. It's year 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will be corrected. So it should be 14th October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This decision was opposed by the deputies of the Serbian Democratic Party and other deputies from the Serb people who were participating in the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so there was a process of outvoting. I'm not a lawyer, so I don't want to go into this constitutional category. But there is one fact I do know. At the time, there was a rule in force at the level of the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina that decisions should be made not by a majority vote but by consensus. Therefore, this outvoting contributed to the fact that an assembly of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina was set up, and this was reflected in the entire political mood prevailing at the time, and this was also evident in Bosanski Samac and Posavina, and all the parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina inhabited by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I note that the answer given is not at all responsive to the question. The question was: What did you learn through your intelligence activities, I think, about the activities of the SDS? And the witness has just given an answer about basically public, publicly known materials, the activities of the Bosnian parliament. The witness please be directed to answer the question that he was asked, or maybe Mr. Pisarevic can clear that up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly. I didn't want to interrupt Mr. Zaric while he was speaking. But it's true that the question that was asked was: What was being done or what the activities were on the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you have just spoken about is public knowledge. All these decisions, policies, and standpoints. What was the behaviour and what were the activities of the Municipal Board, so to say, or the members of the Serbian Democratic Party? What do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, in November, the Serbian Democratic Party, following instructions, organised a plebiscite on the territory of Bosanski Samac for the Serbian people to vote for Bosnia and Herzegovina remaining within Yugoslavia. As far as I know, the Municipal Board of the SDA [as interpreted] carried out certain activities in this direction, and as far as I know, this support was obtained, mostly, of course, from the Serb population in Bosanski Samac, that Bosnia and Herzegovina should remain within Yugoslavia, not excluding the possibility that a small number of people from the Muslim and perhaps the Croatian ethnic communities perhaps also voted in the same way that the Serbs did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Small correction for the transcript. On page 47, line 16, it says: "SDA," and Mr. Zaric was referring to the SDS all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I again raise my earlier objection? The question which Mr. Pisarevic asked Mr. Zaric was not answered. The question was: "What do you know about the activities of the SDS on the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac in your intelligence work? What did you learn about the activities?" Again, the witness has only given answers about a publicly known and publicly organised referendum which was held in Bosnia. That's not the result of intelligence organisation. It's just not responsive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If there was nothing else linked through intelligence services, other than what was in the public activity arena, then you had better say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that you have understood the objections by the Prosecutor and the instruction by the President of the Trial Chamber. So my question is: Did you learn something through your intelligence work about the activities of the Serbian Democratic Party in the territory of Bosanski Samac municipality? If yes, can you tell us what did you learn; if no, if you don't have any knowledge about these activities, say so.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to tackle first thing first. Whether something is intelligence or is a public knowledge, I wouldn't go into that. However, after this referendum, there were other activities on the part of the Serbian Democratic Party. There was the establishment of independent, autonomous regions, there was already in February the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo under foundation. In March there was the election of the top leadership, the parallel leadership, as opposed to the legitimate organs of power which existed in Bosanski Samac. I know that the Serbian Democratic Party had the influence on the recruitment of the reserve policemen in the context that I've already spoken about here. I must also say, not to defend, but when we're talking about the illegal armament of the Serbian Democratic Party, I must say that it was on a much smaller scale in comparison with the other two groups, for one fact, for the fact that the Serbian people officially supported the Yugoslav People's Army as the only defence component, and it would -- and they did not have any other ideological or political position. This was just the way the Serbian people thought, irrespective of their political affiliation. Another thing that I wanted to mention was that some of the illegal arms that arrived in this territory arrived through the young man who went to Croatia, and we know that a lot less Serbian people went to Croatia. Some did, and they went to Knin. When they returned, they did bring weapons, the illegal weapons, but their numbers were much smaller than the numbers of Croats who went to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Samac, Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo under foundation?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question was not given that much attention in the media, although Radio Samac did mention it, and it was mentioned at some political gatherings that I didn't attend. So it was known that the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo were established and that they were composed of some villages from the territory of the municipality of Samac, the municipality of Odzak, Orasje, and Gradacac, because Pelagicevo at that time belonged to Gradacac municipality. I know that -- and I know that that decision, in political terms, among the other two parties and among the people who fostered different political views, stroke a very negative chord. They were of the opinion that such a move and that such a decision of the Serbian Democratic Party and the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Samac was against the positions of the SDA and the HDZ because they fought for the unitarian Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that there were -- that the elections of this assembly, the bodies of this assembly took place?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that. I know that the body's work established and I know that the first president of the assembly of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo was Ilija Ristic. And as far as the election of the Executive Board is concerned, I know that Mirko Jovanovic, who was the legitimate president of the legal authorities of the municipality of Samac and its parliament at that time was later on elected as the president of the Executive Board of the newly elected Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us clarify. Mr. Mirko Jovanovic was the president of the Executive Board [Realtime transcript omitted the words "president of the Executive Board"] of the Municipal Assembly of Samac in which all the political parties had their seats, but he was also the president of the Executive Board of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo, all at the same time?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way I understood it, and in practice that's the way I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that something was misunderstood here. Maybe my colleague could go again through this question with Mr. Zaric. Because if I understood correctly what Mr. Zaric said, he said Mr. Jovanovic, Mirko Jovanovic, was the president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Samac, as well as of the Executive Board of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo. This is how I understood the question, and here it said that Mr. Mirko Jovanovic is the president of the assembly of Bosanski Samac at that time. So maybe we could go through this again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I think it's better for Mr. Simo Zaric to explain clearly who was who.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, can you please explain the role of Mr. Mirko Jovanovic in the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac, pursuant to the elections which took place in 1990. What was his role?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Jovanovic was, after the first multiparty elections, on behalf of the Serbian Democratic Party, was elected the president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Mirko Jovanovic's role in the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that assembly, he was elected as president of the Executive Board of the new Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In practical terms, he had -- this was a parallel political institution with regard to the political institution that I spoke about, which was legally elected in the first multiparty elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who the members of the Executive Board of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo were?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see the decision on the appointment of these people, but I know that the members of the Executive Board were Lazar Mirkic. I know that Milan Simic was one of the members, there was also Mirko Lukic, Stevan Todorovic, Mico Ivanovic, Mijak. I believe -- I can't remember exactly, but I am talking from my perception, from the stories I heard about them being members of the new government of the municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what post was Mr. Stevan Todorovic elected to?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Stevan Todorovic was appointed as the chief of the public security station of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mr. Mico Ivanovic? What post was he appointed to?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was appointed to the post of the commander of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me. Page 52, line 11, answer: "Mr. Stevan Todorovic was appointed as the chief of the public security station," and so on. My question is: Can Mr. Zaric tell us who or which organ appointed him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, and I wish to provide you with a correct answer, I believe that this was at the assembly which was held in the month of March, and this assembly elected the Executive Board and its members, and therefore it was that same assembly, the assembly of the Serbian people, of the Serbian municipalities of Samac and Pelagicevo, was the one that appointed the Executive Board and assigned posts to some people. And pursuant to that decision, Mr. Stevan Todorovic was elected the chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: If you allow me: I'm a bit confused about time and who appointed whom. Can you recall, to the best of your recollection, when Mr. Todorovic was appointed to the position of the chief of the security station? Was it in March or in April? And by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stevan Todorovic was elected at the session of the Assembly which was held in late March, either on the 28th or on the 29th of March. I can't remember exactly. He was elected by the legal assembly which had been established by the Serbian Democratic Party. That means that he was elected by the Assembly of the Serbian people of Samac and Pelagicevo municipalities. The assembly session that was held in Obudovac. This is the information that was available to me and that the media carried at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the other members of the Executive Board? Were they also elected at that session of the Assembly which was held, as you said, either on the 28th or on the 29th of March, 1992? Actually, you didn't mention the year, did you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 28th of March, 1992, and at that session, the Executive Board was elected and all the members of the Executive Board were elected by that session of the Assembly which was active at that time and which was called in the village of Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, when the Territorial Defence of Republika Srpska was established, do you know when that was? When was it established?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I can give you a precise date, but I know one fact: When the state of emergency was declared by the presidency of Republika Srpska, that was on the 15th of April, 1992, it introduced the Territorial Defence as the armed force that was to be put in the defence of the Serbian people. As far as I can remember from what was published, I believe that it was on the 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time also mobilised the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the decision of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina declared a state of emergency, a decision on mobilisation was also adopted, in order to create the Territorial Defence as the only armed force that existed at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Zaric, whether there was a Territorial Defence unit in the municipality of Samac, that is, the Territorial Defence of the Republika Srpska in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Starting not only from the fact that I know that Mr. Mico Ivanovic was appointed commander of the TO at that assembly, but I also know that on the territory of the municipality of Samac, a Territorial Defence did exist. But like many other detachments in the 17th Tactical Group, there was no activity to be noticed. But I know that some companies were established in the local communes. These, however, were not within the composition of the 17th Tactical Group or the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are testifying that on the territory of Bosanski Samac, there was an organised Territorial Defence, as one segment, and that in addition, there was the JNA also?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this, that a Territorial Defence existed in the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had an opportunity to talk about this with Mr. Ivanovic. In a later period, when Mr. Mijak was a member of the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade, along with me, that is, he worked in the command, Mr. Mijak told me he had been appointed commander and that there were certain small Territorial Defence units in some local communes which were not part of the 17th Tactical Group; that he, when the conflict broke out, was in a situation where he had to really become the commander of the Territorial Defence. That's what I learned from the man who carried out this duty. But what extent the Territorial Defence actually functioned is something I could not really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. Just for the sake of clarity of the transcript: Mr. Zaric, in this last answer you've referred to Mr. Ivanovic. But in the transcript, it goes on and then talks about a Mr. Mijak, M-i-j-a-k. Am I correct in assuming that that's Mr. Mico, Mr. Mico Ivanovic, it's not a separate man, spelled M-i-j-a-k? Perhaps you could just clarify with Mr. Zaric, Mr. Pisarevic, that we're talking about one and not two different people here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, when, during your testimony, you mentioned Ivanovic Mijak, then you talk about Mico Ivanovic, is this one and the same person? Are you referring to a single person? Is the person you are talking about called Mico Ivanovic, nicknamed Mijak?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. This is Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Zaric. It's just the way it came out here. Later down the road it might be unclear to us. But you've clarified that, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When talking about the Territorial Defence, what Territorial Defence were you referring to? It's not quite clear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the Serbian Territorial Defence on the territory of the Republic of Serbia and Bosnia and Herzegovina. So I'm referring to the Serbian TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbian Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as you know, until when did the TO of Republika Srpska exist in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It existed until the 12th of May, 1992, when the Peoples's Assembly of Republika Srpska issued a decision on the establishment of the army of Republika Srpska. By that decision, the Serbian Territorial Defence was abolished and all units and staffs belonging to the TO were also abolished, and a single defence component was established under the name of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break now and continue at 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. You continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, we will now talk about an event. Would you, if you know anything about this, tell us about the arrival of members of the Serbian police and a group of specials in the village of Batkusa. What do you know about this event?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that around the 11th of April, or on the 11th of April, 1992, in the village of Batkusa, a group of special purpose soldiers arrived in two military helicopters of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know this, Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard this from my commander, Radovan Antic, on the following day after their arrival, because Commander Antic was in the village and he told me about the arrival of this special purpose unit and the helicopters. And I had another source also, my wife Fatima, who, in the evening on the 11th was returning from Obudovac by car, and she saw these people in camouflage uniforms, so she told me about this. Therefore, this piece of information is reliable, and I believe it was on the 11th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. Mr. Zaric, you mention both Commander Antic and your wife Mrs. Zaric relayed this information to you, but you don't say whether they also told you that the helicopters were JNA helicopters. Your answer seems to refer solely to the people who had arrived. I would be interested to know how you got the information. Was it from Mr. Antic and Mrs. Zaric also concerning the insignia on the two helicopters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That these were helicopters belonging to the JNA, this is something I learned from Commander Antic. He told me this. He said he had information to this effect. He was born in Batkusa and lived there. He resided there, and he often went back there to visit. And he learned this from the local inhabitants, who told him that the specials arrived in JNA helicopters. In the evening of the 11th, my wife, Fatima, driving in her car, only had occasion to see, by the roadside, armed specials in camouflage uniforms, with painted faces and hats on. She didn't know anything about the helicopters. I learned about the helicopters from Commander Antic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else, if anything, did Commander Antic tell you about this?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the commander told us was that they had arrived in Batkusa, that they had landed on the soccer field belonging to the Hijdox [phoen] soccer club of Batkusa, that they had been received by Mr. Todorovic, who at the time, it seems, was performing two duties. He was the chief of the public security station, or [as interpreted] the assistant commander of the 1st Detachment for security and intelligence tasks, and also by Mr. Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is just one word here that I believe changes the meaning of the whole sentence. Mr. Zaric, when he was talking about Witness Todorovic, said he was the chief of the public security station, as well as the assistant, should read, instead "or the assistant," because he was talking about Mr. Todorovic performing two duties at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for the correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And I think there's just also one other thing, in the same paragraph, line 24 of page 58, the sentence concerning Mr. Todorovic's two positions concludes with the words: "And also by Mr. Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak." That really doesn't make sense the way it is printed there in the sentence. Is the implication, Mr. Zaric, that you heard about this from Mr. Ivanovic as well as Mr. Antic, or does it mean something completely different? Maybe you could help us with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think my answer was very precise, so it's obviously an error in interpretation. The information I received from Commander Antic was that these specials were met in Batkusa on the soccer field by Mr. Stevan Todorovic, who at that time was the assistant commander for intelligence and security tasks of the 1st Detachment, and his commander was Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak. And Mr. Todorovic's other duty was that he was appointed chief of the public security station at the session of the 28th of March, which is why I mentioned his two duties. This information that these men were met by Mr. Todorovic and by Mr. Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak, is information I received from my commander, Radovan Antic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to clarify: Mico Ivanovic, also known as Mijak, was the commander of the 1st Detachment, and his command was in Batkusa; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting, but I guess that you, Mr. Pisarevic, will return to the topic. But if not, I want to know whether Mr. Zaric is familiar with the background of those specials, volunteers, or whatever they are called; why and by whom they were arriving in the municipality of Bosanski Samac. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly, Your Honour. We will come to these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Mico Ivanovic, at that moment when he met these specials in Batkusa, also perform two duties?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he performed two duties. At the time, he was the commander of the 1st Detachment, and he was also the commander of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After learning all this, what steps did you take to obtain information about what was going on? Did you have any contacts with Commander Nikolic? What did you talk about with him?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I learned that this team of so-called specials had arrived by helicopter, a day or two after this, rumour started going around about their activities on the ground, which upset people in the municipality and in the town of Samac itself. As a person who was a member of the 4th Detachment, I had to learn what kind of unit this was, because very soon we received information that they were stopping people, stopping buses, stealing money from people in the buses, and I wanted to be informed about this, primarily because on the 12th, in the evening, this issue was raised at the session of the Samac Crisis Staff, the local Crisis Staff. People asked us what sort of men these were, what kind of specials they were, who had arrived by helicopter, and so on and so forth. At this meeting, I said I had no reliable information but that I would do everything in my power to find out what sort of people these were and that I would inform the Crisis Staff about this, and this is what I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me once again, because there are concepts. Page 61 and line 8, the witness, Mr. Zaric, is talking about -- talking about Samac Crisis Staff, the local Crisis Staff. Because this is confusing me. That organ, can you explain what you mean by "the Crisis Staff" at that time, at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, the problem lies in the fact that sometimes you do not finish your sentence to the end. What Crisis Staff? So far we have used the term the local -- the Crisis Staff of the local commune of Samac. When you only say "the Samac Crisis Staff," omitting the word "local commune," this creates confusion. Could you please clarify this for His Honour. What Crisis Staff did you have in mind? What Crisis Staff existed at that time? What Crisis Staff discussed the issue of the specials on the 12th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the local Crisis Staff in the town of Samac, the local Crisis Staff in the town of Samac, that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, this Crisis Staff of the local commune of Samac, did it have any authority over other parts of the municipality or the rest of the territory of the municipality of Samac, or was it just a body covering the town of Samac itself?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Crisis Staff of the local commune of Samac was exclusively in charge of the town of Samac, of that local commune of Samac. The specific feature of this local Crisis Staff, the Crisis Staff of the local commune of Samac, was the fact that very often its meetings were attended by the highest and most responsible people from the political life of the municipality, this for the fact that the town of Samac was the administrative and political centre for the entire municipality and because of that it differed from some other crisis staffs of other local communes which were not that important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's be a bit more precise. The conclusions and the decisions passed at the meetings of this Crisis Staff of that local commune, could they be applied to other local communes, to other parts of the territory of and the municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This Crisis Staff was only in charge of putting forth some proposals and suggestions which were relative to the local commune of the town of Samac itself, and only of that local commune.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: I'm not satisfied by the answers, because as far as we are concerned, the Crisis Staff which we have been talking about so far was formed on the 15th of April, 1992, and now we are talking about some other Crisis Staff. And in order to avoid confusion, I would like to have these concepts cleared. What kind of Crisis Staff is Mr. Zaric now talking about in March and prior to those dates, and the Crisis Staff which we have been talking about prior to listening to Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps if Mr. Zaric told us who the members of this commune Crisis Staff were, it may assist in distinguishing the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And also perhaps, Mr. Zaric, you could tell us again where they met, because if I remember correctly, were they not meeting in the memorial centre, the community centre, the local commune centre? So if we clarify that as well, that will probably help the Trial Chamber on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll try and clarify this situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, can you please remember: How many local communes were there on the territory of Samac municipality?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were 26 local communes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The local commune of the town of Samac was one of those 26 local communes that composed the municipality of Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we are talking about the Crisis Staff of the local commune of Samac, this Crisis Staff existed only for that one local commune, for the local commune of Samac; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, and that body called itself Crisis Staff and it was linked only to the local commune of Samac. All its meetings were held in the pensioners' home that we have mentioned many times here, and this is also the building that housed the local self-government of the municipality of Samac. I have never talked about the Crisis Staff that applied to the level of the entire municipality. Whenever I mentioned the Crisis Staff so far, this was the Crisis Staff of the local commune of the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whatever decisions this Crisis Staff may have issued, and it had another name - it was also called the coordination body - so whatever recommendations it could issue or conclusions it could reach, this all could only be applied in the local commune of the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this could not be applied in any other of the remaining 25 local communes on the territory of Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Likewise, every of the remaining 25 local communes that made up the municipality of Samac could establish their own Crisis Staff; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Every local commune could, and indeed had, its only Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the Crisis Staff, do you mean a body like an advisory body of the local commune?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the word "Crisis Staff of the local commune" was very popular, and that's why I'm using this same term. Every local commune had a Crisis Staff which was composed of the most responsible people from the local administration of that particular local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one more thing, if you could tell us: Who were the members of the coordination body or the Crisis Staff of the local commune of the town of Samac? Who were its members? Who were its active members?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of this coordination body, or the Crisis Staff of the local commune of Samac, were representatives of the advisory body of the local commune of the town of Samac, headed by Safet Hadzialijagic, also known as Pop, who was also the president of that advisory body or council of the local commune; also its members were representatives of the political parties that existed both in the town of Samac, as well as the leaders of the political parties at the level of the municipality, and I was also invited to the meetings of the Crisis Staff by this body, whether you want to call it a coordination body or the Crisis Staff. Whenever I was necessary to attend on behalf of the 4th Detachment. Whenever they invited me, I would respond to the invitation and I would attend the meetings of the Crisis Staff of the local commune of the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The members of this council or the advisory body of the local commune, could they be only the people who resided on the territory of the town of Samac?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, the majority of these people were from the town of Samac itself, but these meetings were sometimes attended by the leaders of the political parties at the level of the municipality. And having said that, I would like to say that sometimes Filip Evic, the president of the HDZ, also attended these meetings, but he resided in Hasic. However, sometimes he would attend the meetings of the local coordination body in the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, I asked you whether the members of the council of the local commune of Samac could only be those people who resided on the territory of the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only them, and nobody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So nobody else could be the member of the council of the local commune of Samac if they resided in the local commune of Hasic Kornica, Pisari, Slatina, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they couldn't. Only those people who resided on the territory of the local commune of Samac could be the members of the council of the local commune of Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me once again, but I think we are, so to say, in the mist. You are talking about the Crisis Staff and council of the local commune of Samac. Could you be so kind, Counsel, to clarify these conceptions as to who is who, and who decided about what, and so on. Because I'm really out in the mist and confused by what Mr. Zaric is telling us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Pisarevic, it would be much clearer if you explain what the various terms -- what various terms were used to describe this local commune Crisis Staff, and thereafter, let's stick to one term.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The local commune of Samac, in other words, the town of Samac, in the municipality of Samac, there are about 24 or 25 villages, and there's also the town of Samac, the urban settlement of Samac. This urban settlement of Samac has its local administration which is called the assembly of the local commune of the town of Samac. This assembly of the local commune of the town of Samac has its executive body. This is the council of the local commune of the town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: But why are you talking about the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll come to that in a minute. This was under the normal circumstances, what I have just explained. Since the situation was getting more complex, the council of the local commune decided that its membership should be expanded and that some new people should become its members, people such as representatives of the town board of the SDA, the local board of the SDP, the local board of the Radical Party, the local board of the reformist forces, and then the local -- the council was not composed of only seven members but rather of twelve members. And then the term "Crisis Staff" became popular. However, at the session of the council, it was said that this would be a coordination body. Mr. Zaric opted for a very awkward term. And this was all in February 1992. And from now on, we are going to use the term "the coordination body of the local commune of the town of Samac," in order to avoid this being mixed up with any other body, with crisis staffs as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, from now on, whenever you refer to this body, you will call it "the coordination body of the local commune of the town of Samac." Mr. Zaric, you've promised the coordination body of the local commune of the town of Samac that you would check the details, that you would find out who these people were, what were their goals, and why they had arrived in the JNA helicopters in Batkusa village. What did you do in order to obtain the information, and after that, did you brief the coordination body of the local commune of the town of Samac on what you had found out?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the 13th of April, together with Commander Antic, I went to the command in Pelagicevo, and on that occasion I spoke directly to Commander Nikolic, and also to Mr. Maksim Simeunovic, my first superior, who was the chief of the intelligence and security organ of the 17th Tactical Group. Mr. Nikolic and Mr. Makso Simeunovic informed us that the group that had arrived was a special purpose group of the police, belonging to the Republic of Serbian Krajina, which arrived in one of the helicopters, while the group that arrived in the other helicopter was a group of lads from the municipality of Samac originally and who had been sent by certain persons or organs for special training, which was carried out in the municipality of Ilok, in Eastern Slavonia, on the territory of the Republic of Croatia, but which at the time was under the control of Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Serb forces," do you mean to say that they were under the control of forces of the Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Republic of Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you once again. There is apparently a mistake on page 68, line 6: "On the 13th of April." It must be the 16th or the 17th, because otherwise it doesn't match with what we have heard before listening to Mr. Zaric. And in addition, I want to know when, at what time of the day, between the 16th and 17th, did you meet Mr. Stevan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honour Lindholm, we're talking about the 13th of April of 1992, because the specials landed, according to the testimonies we've heard so far, on the 11th of April, 1992. Mr. Zaric, true, did go to the command of the 17th also, but we will come to that, because that is another topic not related to the arrival of this special purposes unit. Maybe this is giving rise to confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, please continue. What did the commander tell you when you went to see him, and what did Makso Simeunovic tell you? What information did they give you?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Makso Simeunovic said that on the 11th of April he had been there to meet the helicopters when they brought these specials to Batkusa, that he saw them and he explained what kind of people these were [as interpreted]. Mr. Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One small misunderstanding of Mr. Zaric's words. He said: I wouldn't like to say to meet the helicopters, but here it says that Mr. Makso Simeunovic said that on the 11th of April he had been there to meet the helicopters, suggesting that he was present to meet the person in the helicopter. This is exactly not what Mr. Zaric said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps that can be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zaric, tell us what Mr. Makso Simeunovic told you.

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Simeunovic said that on the 11th he had received information that certain visitors would be arriving in Batkusa and that he should go, and this was a coded message to him from one of his collaborators. When he arrived there at a certain time, precisely at that moment, first one helicopter landed, and the specials got off. They ran out with weapons and demonstrated a drill of theirs, in front of the citizens, because there were also citizens of Batkusa who were present there. And then they set off across the soccer field, in the direction of a youth centre which was not far away from the soccer field. Soon after that, the second helicopter landed and another team arrived, among whom he recognised a certain number of men from the territory of the municipality of Samac. Afterwards, together with the group that was there, he went to the youth centre and he observed a very cordial meeting between the leaders of the group that had arrived and Mr. Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time of day did you and Mr. Antic, on the 13th of April, 1992, go to the command of the 17th Tactical Group in Pelagicevo to see Commander Nikolic and the chief of security, Makso Simeunovic? What time was it?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could have been about 11.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So about 11.00 on the 13th of April?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Commander Nikolic tell you on that occasion? What sort of men were these? Who had arrived?

utterances.speaker: SIMO ZARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic told us that the day before he had had an official meeting in Donji Zabar, on the premises of the company Agro Posavina, with representatives of these units that had arrived, and their leaders, at least at the time, were people we knew only by nickname, Crni and Debeli, and that among others, Mr. Blagoje Simic, Stevan Todorovic, and some others whose names I can't remember were present, and that he had been told that they introduced themselves and said that they were policemen of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. The other part of the unit were local men who had gone for training, but neither he nor Mr. Nikolic, as the commander of the 17th Tactical Group, knew about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been told that I should conclude with my examination-in-chief now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because there's a matter the Trial Chamber wants to deal with. This is regarding the motion by the Prosecution dated 28th April on Rule 71 depositions. The Trial Chamber was waiting for the response from the Defence counsel on this one, and the information was given through the legal officer. But then when the other motion was discussed, we didn't get the response of the Defence counsel. So we wanted to find out whether there is anything they wish to say or they have nothing to contribute. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. If my understanding is correct, we have to give our response on Prosecution motion dated April 28th, under the title "Motion reference to admission into evidence of Rule 71 depositions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, just for the record, in response to our learned friend's motion, in paragraph 4 of the motion, page 3, there is expression that on 17th of April, 2003, the Trial Chamber -- I made a quote of this motion "without specific objection from the accused." And then in paragraph 6 of the same motion, the expression used by the Prosecution that "the accused did not object to the admission of the depositions into evidence." At least it's not fair and correct, since the Defence acted fully in accordance and upon the ruling of this Honourable Trial Chamber. And needless to say that prior to the process of deposition under the Rule 71 of the Rules, Defence raised a substantial issue and submissions with that regard. The arguments by the Defence were denied by this Honourable Trial Chamber. Then the Defence filed a request for the certification under the Rule 73. This request was also denied by this Honourable Trial Chamber. So in conclusion, my learned friend will add their submissions speaking on behalf of my client: In conclusion, we -- Defence for Dr. Blagoje Simic has nothing to add to our previous submissions with that particular regard. Everything was raised in our oral submissions, as well as in our request for certification. And frankly, we can only speculate the reasons why our learned friend raised that issue, but there is nothing new for the Defence with that regard. We are compiling and we are absolutely concur with the previous rulings of this Honourable Trial Chamber. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, before you speak, Mr. Lukic: Mr. Pantelic, I have a question as to whether we are in fact looking at the same motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I know dated the 28th of April, 2003. I'm interested, though, in knowing what the Defence position is on the relief sought in the Prosecution's motion, which can be found on page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Under the paragraph 7, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Under paragraph 7, where, as you can see, it says that they request the Trial Chamber ascertain from an accused who did not call a witness whose deposition has been admitted into evidence whether he wants to cross-examine that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We already gave our answers in our oral submissions in our request for certification. So I don't want to repeat. So Defence stands with all previous submissions in oral submission, prior to deposition process, and in our request for certification. Nothing new, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So yesterday, then, when you responded concerning the motion by the Prosecution to allow for Mr. Erletic to be brought here for cross-examination, Mr. Lukic said no, on behalf of his client, Mr. Tadic, but you said yes, on behalf of your client, Dr. Blagoje Simic. So what I just want to get clear is: In this more general motion, which is with respect to all of the Rule 71 deposition witnesses, your position is that you don't want to ask for any of them to be brought for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, Your Honour, it is not the case. As I said, I am standing fully with my previous oral submissions and my request for the certification, and I have to respect the order by this Honourable Trial Chamber. So everything has been done. It's something absolutely -- I don't know how to understand this motion. Is it a kind of reconsideration of your previous ruling or whatever? I mean, as I said, we are standing fully in accordance with our previous submissions, oral submissions and our written request for certification, simple as that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do not wish to repeat what Mr. Pantelic said, but I will try to explain in other words. However, I fully support the position of Mr. Pantelic. It is simply not clear to me what the Prosecution now wants from the Defence that the Defence has not already stated. If we have to say again whether we agree to cross-examination in general of all the witnesses whose depositions were taken, we have already explained our standpoint and the Trial Chamber has already issued its decision. These two cases concerning Mr. Marko Tubakovic and Mr. Erletic, I have already replied as to whether I or the Defence of Mr. Tadic will cross-examine. As for the cross-examination of other deposition witnesses, there is nothing I can add to what has already been said. I simply feel that we have put forward our position and that we have nothing further to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On behalf of Mr. Zaric's Defence, I would like to say that we share the same position in this case as Mr. Tadic and Mr. Blagoje Simic Defence. We already filed a joint motion asking for certification about a ruling the Trial Chamber made. We have nothing new to add to this motion. And we also supported the oral submission of Mr. Lukic when this topic was raised before this Trial Chamber. So there is nothing new that we could add to these submissions. So we are sharing the same position as all other Defences in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution briefly respond to this, Your Honour? It seems like there's some real misunderstanding on the part of the Defence as to the purpose in our filing this motion and what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we allow you to speak --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is of the view that the motion by the Prosecution is quite clear, and it doesn't think that there is any need for the Prosecution to reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I don't reply, could I ask an inquiry -- I'm not quite sure as to what the Defence is saying. It seems to be contradictory, and I think Judge Williams has appointed that out, on the one hand they wish to cross-examine Mr. Tubakovic and Mr. Erletic. We are asking whether they wish to cross-examine any other witnesses whose evidence has been admitted into evidence. The answers, with respect to my friends, is unclear and could I ask the Trial Chamber to ask them again so it's completely clear: Do they wish to cross-examine any witnesses whose evidence have been admitted into evidence, or are they waiving or saying they do not wish to cross-examine? That's what the motion is asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber will consider what the parties have said and will make our ruling in due course. Mr. Pisarevic, for purposes of planning, we wanted to find out how long you think Mr. Zaric still has to complete the evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At least five days, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean -- because today is the second day, so you mean you need another three days?

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I need another five days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is he going to discuss? It's just his defence in the -- in his efforts to meet his allegations in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But Mr. Zaric's interview contains about 300 pages. When planning the defence of Mr. Zaric, everything that he was asked about by the investigators and everything he said in his interview, and also the time period covered by the indictment and the mention of Mr. Zaric in various situations, in view of all this, I don't want to limit the time for Mr. Zaric to testify about everything that touches upon his activities in the relevant period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, the point is that: Yes, we've looked at the interviews. Some of the matters are not relevant to the indictment and some of the matters are completely outside the allegations in the indictment. So what the Trial Chamber is asking is that he should limit his defence to indictment against him, the particulars and the allegations in the indictment against him, not necessarily everything that was raised during the interrogations with the Prosecutor, or indeed every detail of everything else covered in that material time. It's just the defence that -- the evidence supporting his defence that the Trial Chamber is interested in. So perhaps you may consider that approach. We shall adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 7th day of May 2003, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
